frontier.hypothesis: F16 — close the parameter's allocno priority into the open interval (200, 306) on the zero-lever goto-loop chassis and it lands target's exact $s0/$s1/$s2/$s3 map with no lever of any kind.
frontier.mechanism: The whole 18-point residual is one demotion: the parameter pseudo must sort below D_800A1494 (pri 306) and above D_800A11DC (pri 200) in global.c:allocno_compare, after which find_reg hands out target's map. pri = nrefs*10000/livelen, verified to the integer on all four allocnos. Route (a) is param livelen 52 -> 66..99 at nrefs 2; route (b) is both pointers nrefs 3 -> 4. This session killed the dead-store spelling of (b) and the statement-order spelling of (a).
frontier.next_probe: First find out WHY the parameter's livelen is only 52 when the three pointers are 96-100 on the same body — it is set in the prologue and consumed by the loop-back test at the very bottom, so ~100 is what one would expect. Read the ';; Function saEft01Init' section of tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s8/g0/system.i.lreg together with flow.c's live-range walk that produces reg_live_length, and identify the region the param is NOT live in. That region is the lever surface: a C spelling that keeps the parameter live across it moves livelen into the window directly, with no FAKE-family construct. Screen with tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s8/score.py, confirm with the greg 'Register dispositions' line from s8/idump.sh.

frontier.hypothesis: F17 — a LIVE fourth reference to D_800A125C and D_800A1494 puts them at pri 416 and 408, above the parameter's 384, preserving their relative order and landing target's map.
frontier.mechanism: Route (b) of F16. Both pointers sit at nrefs 3 (one set, two uses). H35 proved the extra reference must survive flow.c, so it has to be a real use whose value is consumed — no dead store, no self-assign, no declaration-only construct.
frontier.next_probe: The constraint is tight: the function only reads D_800A125C[Intr.sync] and D_800A125C[Intr.ready], so a fourth reference has to come from a restructuring that genuinely consumes the pointer again. Price the duplicated-statement-into-arms family on the `check:` if-chain first — it is BB2's sanctioned byte-neutral ref-lift and the only construct measured to move reg_n_refs where dead stores do not. Measure it before deciding whether it is proposable; it would need byte-neutrality verification, the lever-exhaustion record (sessions 1-8 now supply it) and a /* FAKE */ annotation.

frontier.hypothesis: F18 — the loop.c asymmetry, now correctly scoped: address movables move in the original compile, single-use const_int movables do not.
frontier.mechanism: Session 8's read of the target bytes narrows the inherited F13. The original compile DID run LICM (all three symbol addresses are hoisted into the pre-loop block as $s0/$s1/$s3) and did NOT move the two const_int movables, so the question is no longer 'how do we suppress LICM' but 'what distinguishes an address movable from a single-use const_int movable in scan_loop/move_movables'. Candidate answer: each const_int is used EXACTLY ONCE, which is the precondition of the 'large loop lossage' substitution path in loop.c (the block after the '/* A potential lossage ... */' comment around loop.c:725, reached only in a loop containing calls — this loop contains four).
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:725-840 and determine what happens to a single-use const_int movable in a loop-with-calls when validate_replace_rtx of the constant into its slt/and use FAILS (0x3C0000 and 0x1000000 are outside MIPS's 16-bit immediate range, and the slt pattern wants a register in that operand anyway). If the movable is dropped rather than moved, the real-loop chassis can be made to behave like target legitimately and cleank's 21/90 map becomes reachable without k. Do this only if F16/F17 do not close, since the goto-loop chassis reaches the same map with no LICM question at all.
